sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cáer, also set as Cáer Ibormeith, stands as an Irish heroine or goddess. The sweet god of verse, Aonghus Og, loved her. In a dream he was shown at last a woman he had never glanced upon; so sharp was his longing that he chased her through every land. Plan at the Lake of the Dragon's Outlet lay she, surfacing as a swan hung with one hundred and thirty gold loops. Aongus did as much, turning also into a swan, and flying, they nested off together, singing so liquid that every hearer dropped asleep for three nights' long. W. B. Yeats's 'The Song of Wandering Ae' draws directly on the romance.

okr.objective: Cáer is a swan maiden beloved of the poet god Aonghus.
key_results: Cáer is a heroine or goddess of Irish legend.
Aonghus the god of poetry searched the world for her.
He met her as a swan on the Lake of Dragon's Mouths.
The pair flew away together and their song brought sleep.
